name: First Ottoman Siege of Constantinople
summary: Sultan Murad II besieges Constantinople in 1422, the first major Ottoman attempt to take the city since Timur's defeat of the Ottomans in 1402. The siege fails, the Theodosian Walls hold, and a palace revolt in Anatolia forces Murad to withdraw. The Byzantine Empire, reduced to Constantinople and a few nearby territories, demonstrates that its walls are still impregnable to Ottoman forces without adequate siege artillery.

_quarry.structural_significance: The 1422 failure underscores why the 1453 conquest required Mehmed II's massive artillery investment; the siege also reveals the Byzantine Empire's complete military and political exhaustion, only the walls protect a state that can no longer field an army; the 31 years between 1422 and 1453 are Byzantine negotiations for western Christian aid that never materializes in sufficient force
